A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TraitBasis and τ-Trait research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.6 support reliable comparison. The appendices match apart from numbering and presentation details.

before.justification: V1 reports original human and LLM-judge evaluations, agent stress-test results, and supplementary trait analyses in Tables 2–6 and Appendix A.3.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds simulator controls, Qwen evaluations, GPT-5 stress-test results, and modified BFCL measurements.

M1.justification: Contrastive activation averaging, human-guided layer selection, scaled activation addition, and linear trait composition remain unchanged. V2's explicit four-pair explanation does not establish a procedural change: v1 already reports four samples and supplies corresponding examples.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluation on the 200-task BFCL multi-turn base function-calling subset, extending coverage beyond the previously evaluated conversational settings. The original airline, retail, telecom, and telehealth domains, along with TalkMap/MSDialog training data, remain.

E2.justification: The methods evaluated against TraitBasis remain prompting, SFT, and LoRA, with LoRA excluded from composition in both versions. The Qwen evaluation reuses SFT. GPT-5 is an additional agent being tested, while new Table 2 compares unsteered user simulators; neither introduces a new competing trait-induction method.

E3.justification: New protocols include intent-preserving BFCL task rephrasing with AST-based function-call matching, RQ1–RQ3 replication on Qwen3-8B, and controls holding the GPT-4o assistant fixed while changing the unsteered user model. GPT-5 is also added to τ-Trait evaluation. The original conversation counts, lengths, annotation procedures, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds several validation questions: whether one versus four contrastive pairs suffices, whether unsteered Llama and GPT-4o users produce comparable assistant performance, and whether TraitBasis advantages transfer to Qwen. The pair-count ablation is reported only qualitatively. Existing stability, composition, and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 100 shuffled Elo calculations, the same Elo uncertainty entries, and three-run averaging for τ-Trait. The added BFCL results follow the same three-rollout averaging practice. No new seed disclosure, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Original matched results remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial outcomes. Table 5 adds GPT-5, including a −62.6% retail/impatience entry; Table 6 reports BFCL average changes of −55.94% for GPT-4o and −66.25% for Kimi K2. Section 6.1 adds Qwen results, including 73.75% versus 50% fidelity for TraitBasis versus SFT. These are additional settings, not improvements over matched v1 runs.

T1.justification: The persona definitions, activation averaging and contrastive-difference equations, trait matrix, and τ-Trait POMDP formulation remain mathematically equivalent. V2 reformats an equation and adds conceptual explanations without introducing or revising a formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The central TraitBasis and τ-Trait contributions remain. V2 explicitly claims generalization across Llama and Qwen in the introduction and includes modified BFCL in the conclusion. The abstract changes the stated average degradation range from 2%–30% to 4%–20%, without reconciling that summary with the expanded results.

C2.justification: New Section 8 substantively qualifies behavioral coverage, backbone-specific vector extraction, and untested model scales. Section 3.2 adds an explanation that contrastive examples probe existing trait representations rather than teach traits. V2 also interprets BFCL results as suggesting consistent trait-specific difficulties across agents. Earlier interpretations of fading, blending, and LLM-judge limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies previously absent core implementation information: the Llama-3.1-8B backbone and baseline training on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct for three epochs, learning rate 2×10^-5, cosine scheduling, and LoRA rank 128. These are new disclosures, not evidence of changed retained runs. The repository address remains, but the abstract now inconsistently states both planned and completed open-sourcing.

R1.justification: A focused new subsection connects TraitBasis to sparse autoencoders and feature discovery, citing Templeton, Elhage, Bayat, and Deng while distinguishing contrastive extraction from learned sparse dictionaries. Ye et al.'s RotBench is also added. The broader positioning around activation steering for persistent user simulation remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method exposition, experimental descriptions, and results discussion undergo extensive paragraph-level rewriting. V2 adds a cross-model discussion and standalone Limitations section. This is widespread language revision beyond the insertion of new scientific content; appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds simulator-control and BFCL tables, expands and reformats the τ-Trait table, and redisplays the existing appendix fidelity results as main-text Table 4 while retaining them as Table 7. Figure 1's caption expands, but the underlying figures and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The BFCL and Qwen evaluations address generalization gaps, while previously missing backbone/training details and explicit limitations improve reproducibility and scope clarity. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: the conclusion retains a 46% maximum despite new table entries showing 62.6% and 80% declines, and the abstract simultaneously plans and claims open-sourcing. The added validation is useful, but the revision does not consistently reconcile its claims with its evidence.
